Write SCENE LS1 (1 of 7) of a natural Thai LISTENING conversation between two people for a learner.
WHOLE CONVERSATION: two friends meet, catch up and talk about everyday things (numbers & prices, shopping & payment, food & cooking)
SPEAKERS: A = Speaker A (friend) · B = Speaker B (friend) · A = a man: ผม for "I", every sentence ends with ครับ. B = a woman: ฉัน for "I", ends with ค่ะ (statement) or คะ (question).
REGISTER: natural spoken · polite particles: A ครับ · B ค่ะ/คะ
THIS SCENE: A and B meet, greet each other and start talking about today
ONE CONVERSATION — the learner hears ONE continuous conversation; this request writes its next PART (part 1, internal only — never announce it).
CONVERSATION CONTRACT: speakers A = Speaker A (friend) · B = Speaker B (friend) · relationship: friends · opening location: where they meet · objective: spend time together: meet → decide where to go → agree the time → go there → do / eat / buy → pay → say goodbye · ending goal: they finish what they set out to do and say goodbye
STORY SO FAR: (nothing yet — this part opens the conversation)
NEXT PART GOAL: see THIS SCENE above.
- Do NOT say goodbye: the conversation continues afterwards. End this part on an answer or a statement, not on an open question.
LATER PARTS will use: ไปที่, น่าดู, ที่นั่น, นักท่องเที่ยว, พิพิธภัณฑสถานแห่งชาติ, สนามหลวง, สิบเอ็ดโมงเช้า, สิบโมงเช้า, หมายถึง, ตลก, ไม่เชิง, รถแท็กซี่, ทาง, นานเท่าไหร่, คือ, ทานกันเลย, ผัดไทย, ร้านอาหาร, ขนาด, พัน, ใบเสร็จ, บัตร, นม, เบอร์โทรศัพท์, โชคดี (leave them for later).
SCENE INTENT: WHO the same two friends throughout · WHERE where they meet · SITUATION A and B meet, greet each other and start talking about today · WHY they talk: spend time together: meet → decide where to go → agree the time → go there → do / eat / buy → pay → say goodbye · WHAT they want to achieve: A and B meet, greet each other and start talking about today. Every turn moves this goal on; a target that does not fit the goal is used in a short natural aside, never a random topic jump.
CONTEXT SO FAR: this is the opening scene — start with a natural greeting
SCENE SHAPE: the exchanges pursue the scene goal; the scene ENDS with that goal resolved (they decide, agree, pay, or say goodbye). Lesson words are heard inside real talk — never a list of sentences about each word.
CLOSED WORLD — PRIORITY ORDER: 1. use ONLY the vocabulary listed here · 2. use every required target · 3. correct grammar · 4. the learner level · 5. be natural WITHIN those limits. Naturalness never justifies a word that is not listed.
THIS SCENE MUST USE ALL OF THESE 5 REQUIRED TARGET WORDS (id | word [reading] | meaning | role) — every one must appear in the actual text of a turn:
T787 | พวกคุณ [phûak-khun] | you all | CONTENT
T719 | แก่ [gâe] | old (people, living things) | DESCRIPTION
T717 | คุณอายุเท่าไหร่ [khun-aa-yú-thâo-rài] | how old are you? | QUESTION_WORD
T737 | เป็นอย่างไร [pen-yàang-rai] | how is it? | QUESTION_WORD
T1152 | ศูนย์ [sǔun] | centre (intended sense: zero — the number 0 (phone numbers ศูนย์แปด…, scores, temperatures) (NOT: the "centre" sense (ศูนย์การค้า) is a different meaning; never an implausible zero price)) | CONTENT
ALLOWED SUPPORT VOCABULARY (already taught — the ONLY other content words you may use; any inflected form of them is fine): คุณ (you) · มา (come) · ไป (go) · เหรอ (really?) · จริง (true) · จริงเหรอ (really?) · มาก (very) · เท่าไหร่ (how much) · อย่างไร (how) · สิ ((urging particle) go on, do it) · คะ (polite question particle (female)) · ค่ะ (polite particle (female)) · ครับ (polite particle (male)) · ปี (year) · เป็น (to be (identity) · รับ (receive) · รอ (wait) · อายุ (age) · จะ (will) · สิบ (ten)
ALLOWED GRAMMAR / FUNCTION WORDS (particles, copula, inflection, sentence endings): ครับ ค่ะ คะ นะ ก็ ที่ ของ กับ ใน ไม่ ได้ จะ อ้อ อ๋อ อืม เอ่อ ค่า คับ จ้ะ จ้า จ๊ะ น่ะ นะคะ นะครับ ครับผม ขา จ๋า สิ ซิ เถอะ หรอก แหละ เนอะ ล่ะ ละ จัง ไหม มั้ย เหรอ หรอ หรือเปล่า ไหมคะ ไหมครับ
You may use ONLY: 1. the required target words · 2. the allowed support vocabulary · 3. the grammar / function words. Do NOT introduce any other lexical content (no other noun, verb, adjective, adverb, interjection or name). If an idea cannot be said with these words, SIMPLIFY THE IDEA — never improvise a new word.
TURN PLAN — MEANING FIRST, VERBALIZABILITY PROVEN (validated before this call; say each planned turn in this order, with exactly this meaning; at most ONE extra short reaction may be added between planned turns):
PROVEN FRAME = a sentence already checked for this learner (every word authorised, within the length limit, the lesson word present): say it like this or as a natural variant with the SAME words, and keep the track register.
  T1 A QUESTION(age) — A asks B how old (using คุณอายุเท่าไหร่ "how old are you?") · REQUIRED: คุณอายุเท่าไหร่ "how old are you?" · SUPPORT: คุณ มา ไป เหรอ จริง จริงเหรอ · PROVEN: คุณอายุเท่าไหร่ครับ
  T2 B ANSWER — B answers with an age ⟨must give an age⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: คุณ มา ไป เหรอ จริง จริงเหรอ · PROVEN: สิบปีค่ะ
  T3 A QUESTION(how it is) — A asks B how it is (using เป็นอย่างไร "how is it?" + ศูนย์ "centre") · REQUIRED: เป็นอย่างไร "how is it?" + ศูนย์ "centre" · SUPPORT: คุณ มา ไป เหรอ จริง จริงเหรอ · PROVEN: ศูนย์เป็นอย่างไรครับ
  T4 B ANSWER — B answers with how it is (using แก่ "old (people, living things)") ⟨must give how it is⟩ · REQUIRED: แก่ "old (people, living things)" · SUPPORT: คุณ มา ไป เหรอ จริง จริงเหรอ · PROVEN: แก่มากค่ะ
  T5 A STATEMENT — A tells B something about พวกคุณ "you all" · REQUIRED: พวกคุณ "you all" · SUPPORT: คุณ มา ไป เหรอ จริง จริงเหรอ · PROVEN: พวกคุณจะไปร้านครับ
  T6 B REACTION — B reacts ⟨must give a reaction to it⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: คุณ มา ไป เหรอ จริง จริงเหรอ · PROVEN: จริงเหรอคะ
PLAN: exchange 1: A uses คุณอายุเท่าไหร่, then B replies · exchange 2: A uses เป็นอย่างไร+ศูนย์, then B uses แก่ · exchange 3: A uses พวกคุณ, then B replies
ROLE GUIDE: CONTENT = the topic of a turn · DESCRIPTION = a reaction or comment on something · QUESTION_WORD = a question the other speaker answers
LENGTH: 6–7 turns. HARD MAXIMUM 7 turns.
EACH TURN: CURRENT LEVEL: 10th Kyu · PREFERRED LENGTH: 3–5 Thai words · ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM: 7 Thai words (polite / question / sentence-final particles do not count). Prefer 3–5 — the shortest natural way to say it. Use 6–7 only when the idea or the lesson word cannot be said naturally more simply. Never exceed 7. A short natural reply ("yes", "okay", "really?") is fine — never pad a line. If a speaker needs to say more, split it into another turn. Keep the situation simple enough to say at this level — one idea per turn (e.g. "How much is it?" / "Ten thousand baht." / "That is expensive."), never explanations in one long turn.
RULES:
- Each turn is ONE speaker; questions get answers; never put a question and its answer in the same turn; A and B both speak.
- At most 3 lesson words per turn (the required words above AND these other lesson words count: หมายถึง, บัตร, ทานกันเลย, ขนาด, พัน, นม, นักท่องเที่ยว, น่าดู, ใบเสร็จ, สิบโมงเช้า, นานเท่าไหร่, รถแท็กซี่, ไปที่, คือ, ตลก, พิพิธภัณฑสถานแห่งชาติ, สนามหลวง, ไม่เชิง, สิบเอ็ดโมงเช้า, ทาง, โชคดี, ที่นั่น, ผัดไทย, ร้านอาหาร, เบอร์โทรศัพท์).
- Response words (yes / no / yeah …) are used as REPLIES. No repeated sentences. No filler turns that do nothing.
- Do not say goodbye yet; the conversation continues in the next scene.
- Content words ONLY from the required targets and the ALLOWED SUPPORT VOCABULARY above. No personal names.

You are a native Thai speaker checking learner material. For EACH sentence answer: would a native speaker plausibly say this exact sentence in ordinary conversation, with this intended meaning, as this speaker?
Penalise: malformed grammar, target-word stuffing, duplicated words, English-shaped Thai, wrong sense of a word, mixed male/female particles (ผม/ครับ vs ฉัน/ค่ะ/คะ), absurd everyday claims, meaningless fragments.
For a learner, short, ordinary, native-sounding speech is BETTER than elaborate native-like phrasing: do NOT reward conjunction chains, repeated subjects, several ideas in one sentence, verbose explanations, or formal wording where simpler speech exists. A short complete reply ("yes", "okay, let's go", "really?") is fully natural.
JUDGE IN CONTEXT. Grammatical possibility is not enough (an everyday hotel price of zero baht, สิบพัน instead of หนึ่งหมื่น, "let's stand" with no reason to stand are not useful Thai), but a common everyday word is NOT unnatural just because a more colloquial alternative exists: never reject a sentence for a word being "formal" unless that word is genuinely written / literary Thai. When s < 4 you MUST give "construction" (the exact Thai span that is wrong, copied from the sentence), "reason" (the specific linguistic problem) and "alternative" (an idiomatic Thai sentence for the same meaning that still uses the target word). Stylistic preference is s=4, not a rejection.
THAI LEXICAL FACTS: จ่าย (pay) is ordinary spoken Thai, never "too formal". 10,000 is หนึ่งหมื่น / หมื่น (สิบพัน is not idiomatic). พอดี means "just right / fits / exactly enough" (and พอดี… at the start = "it so happens"); English "just right" does NOT require เพิ่ง (เพิ่ง = "just" in time: has just happened). เจอ + a person = "meet / see"; เจอ + a thing = "find". พี่ can ADDRESS the listener ("you", someone a little older) or mean "older sibling" — judge which by context; either is correct Thai. หน่อย softens a request or asks for "a bit more" (ช่วยหน่อย, เร็วหน่อย); it does not attach to a descriptive adjective to mean "quite". A price of zero baht is only credible when something is free. A speaker variation that is merely stylistic is never an error.
Scale: 5 natural · 4 natural with a small quirk · 3 understandable but unnatural · 2 wrong/awkward · 1 broken.

When s < 4 also give "issue": "SENTENCE_UNNATURAL" (this sentence is badly built — another sentence could use the target naturally), "TARGET_USAGE_UNSUITABLE_FOR_REGISTER" (the TARGET WORD ITSELF is wrong for casual spoken conversation: formal, written, archaic), or "TARGET_CANONICAL_ENTRY_SUSPECT" (the target expression itself is not a normal expression for its meaning).

THAI LEXICAL FACTS: จ่าย (pay) is ordinary spoken Thai, never "too formal". 10,000 is หนึ่งหมื่น / หมื่น (สิบพัน is not idiomatic). พอดี means "just right / fits / exactly enough" (and พอดี… at the start = "it so happens"); English "just right" does NOT require เพิ่ง (เพิ่ง = "just" in time: has just happened). เจอ + a person = "meet / see"; เจอ + a thing = "find". พี่ can ADDRESS the listener ("you", someone a little older) or mean "older sibling" — judge which by context; either is correct Thai. หน่อย softens a request or asks for "a bit more" (ช่วยหน่อย, เร็วหน่อย); it does not attach to a descriptive adjective to mean "quite".
